prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1162; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. Insured vehicle sustained front bumper and grille damage. Claimant vehicle reported front-end contact with minor deformation. Both drivers reported at scene. Police report requested. Claimant reports knee pain and has retained counsel; all further contact to be routed through attorney's office.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office. Confirmed representation letter received and filed. Attorney requested full liability investigation before any settlement discussion. Asked for copies of photos, recorded statement from insured, and vehicle inspection report. Acknowledged in writing. Medical authorization requested from attorney for claimant's knee treatment records.

Entry 3: Vehicle inspections completed for both vehicles. Insured vehicle estimate reviewed and approved for repair. Claimant vehicle shows crushed bumper cover and cracked headlamp assembly, consistent with reported impact speed. Photos uploaded to file. Recorded statement from insured obtained; insured states the other vehicle crossed into their lane shortly before impact, which is in conflict with claimant's account.

Entry 4: Received medical records from claimant's treating provider via attorney. Diagnosis indicates soft tissue injury to the left knee with swelling and limited range of motion. Physical therapy recommended. Attorney submitted demand package requesting review. Referred file to bodily injury unit for evaluation. Liability still disputed pending review of police report and intersection camera footage.

Entry 5: Police report received; it lists the claimant's vehicle as having failed to yield on the left turn. Intersection camera footage requested from the municipality, not yet received. Reserves reviewed and adjusted for bodily injury exposure. Diary set for follow-up with claimant's attorney in two weeks to request updated treatment status and footage status.
